To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fermented legumes (M. vulgaris) was the best protein source among the legumes tested in terms of protein quality and quantity.
germinated and fermented all legume mixed protein diets in rats can be used as good quality protein diets.
germinated and fermented legumes can be used to produce high quality protein diets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nutritional evaluation of germinated and fermented under-utilized legumes.
the nutritional evaluation of germinated, dried and fermented all legume mixed protein diets in rats.
the development and evaluation of the nutritional quality of mixed underutilized legume diets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
germinated, fermented, dried and mixed underutilized legume protein diets are good sources of protein for animal consumption.
the best diet was diet MVD 64, which was a diet made of Mucuna vulgar is germinated (62hr), fermented (62hr) and dried at a temperature of 65°C (57.5°C).
the fermented Mucuna vulgarus (MVD 57.5) diet was most superior to the other diets in all the performance characteristics determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fermented legumes are superior to germinated and dried legumes for protein production.
fermented legumes are better than germinated legumes and that germinated legumes are better that the ungerminated (dried) ones.
germination and fermentation improved the protein quality of the legumes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the germination and fermentation processes are effective in improving the protein quality of underutilized legume seeds.
germination and fermentation are good methods to improve the nutritive value of legume seeds.
germination, fermentation and drying of legumes can enhance the nutritional value and utilization of the protein in the diet.
